runs.text: A critical number is an interior point where f' is zero or does not exist, provided f itself is defined there.

A differentiable function is increasing where f' > 0 and decreasing where f' < 0. It is convex (concave up) on an interval when its secant slopes increase; f'' >= 0 is a common sufficient criterion when f'' exists.

blocks.tex: f'(c)=0,\ f''(c)>0\Rightarrow\text{strict local minimum};\qquad f''(c)<0\Rightarrow\text{strict local maximum}

runs.text: For a continuous function on a closed interval, global extrema occur among endpoints and interior critical numbers. The first derivative sign change is often stronger than the second derivative test.

items.text: The second derivative test requires f'(c)=0 and f''(c) to exist; f''(c)=0 is inconclusive.
A change in concavity is required for an inflection point; f''=0 alone is not enough.
Endpoints must be checked in closed-interval optimization.
